trend.title: Green Street: Commercial Property Prices Fall 0.7% in October, Trimming 12-Month Gain to 3.7%
trend.scope: U.S. commercial real estate values (Green Street Commercial Property Price Index, October 2026)
trend.metric: All-property index -0.7% in October; +3.7% over twelve months
trend.summary: Green Street reports that its Commercial Property Price Index declined 0.7 percent in October 2026, leaving values up 3.7 percent over the past twelve months. The firm's co-head of strategic research said a recent dip in bond yields is a welcome sign but that investors are still contending with a 10-year Treasury yield near 5 percent.
trend.significance: A monthly price decline with long-term rates near 5 percent keeps pressure on appraised values that drive loan-to-value tests, refinancing proceeds and maturity extensions. Where updated appraisals come in lower, borrowers face paydown demands, cash-management triggers and covenant defaults, and the gap between valuation and debt is what typically pushes a workout toward receivership or foreclosure litigation. Owners and lenders heading into 2027 maturities should expect valuation disputes to feature in extension and modification fights.

verification.claim: The index is up 3.7% over the past twelve months
verification.quote: Over the past twelve months, the index has increased 3.7%.

verification.claim: Investors are dealing with a 10-year Treasury close to 5%
verification.quote: investors are still dealing with a 10-year Treasury that is close to 5%
